claim: Final metric is pooled row-level RMSE.
implication: All CV aggregation must pool scored rows; per-well averages are diagnostic only.

claim: Hidden test contains roughly 200 wells; visible test contains only a few train-derived authoring examples.
implication: Visible test overlap cannot validate hidden-test generalization.

claim: Training has 773 wells and every simulated target mask is a suffix.
implication: Use whole-well hidden-suffix simulation.

claim: Last-known-TVT continuation has about 15.91 pooled RMSE locally.
implication: Every formulation must beat this and report delta.

claim: Most high-frequency TVT variation is inherited from known trajectory; smooth U=TVT+Z is the main target.
implication: Model U level/trend and convert back to TVT.

claim: A small fraction of wells dominates squared error.
implication: Report worst-well and SSE concentration metrics for every run.

claim: Per-well mean/datum error explains a large fraction of SSE.
implication: Decompose residual into datum, trend and shape.

claim: Aggregate grouped CV ordering can invert on the public leaderboard.
implication: Require controls, repeated folds, harsher splits and final-family diversity.

claim: A weak standalone model can improve a strong ensemble when residual correlation is low.
implication: Optimize ensemble weights on OOF residual covariance, not standalone score.

claim: Individually validated corrections can harm when stacked.
implication: Test every component in final placement and retain negative configurations.

claim: Risk detection is easier than predicting the signed correction direction.
implication: Do not actuate a gate without signed-direction evidence.

claim: Copied notebook uses seven named external datasets and one opaque mount.
implication: Treat it as an idea catalogue, not a reproducible baseline.

claim: Three named notebook datasets show unknown licenses.
implication: Quarantine those artifacts pending license/provenance resolution.

claim: Participants report tabular, non-tabular and pure-physics systems in the 5.x–6.x range.
implication: Maintain multiple formulation tracks; do not copy undisclosed claims.

claim: Known-prefix typewell alignment quality has local correlation about 0.454 with hidden oracle quality.
implication: Use alignment quality as a feature/gate, not as definitive selector.

claim: Hidden-zone GR missingness is substantial and highly variable.
implication: Add missingness-aware regimes and no-GR fallbacks.

claim: Across all 773 training wells, hidden-label oracle constant and line paths score 9.0354 and 6.6972, while a robust smooth curve scores 3.1106.
implication: A gold-targeting legal bank must recover nonlinear whole-tail shape; datum-only and line-only optimization are insufficient.

claim: Pilkwang's fixed PF/beam selector scores 10.5831 pooled RMSE and its worst decile contributes 61.95% of SSE.
implication: Measure candidate oracle coverage separately from legal selector regret and catastrophe probability.

claim: Heel affine GR calibration worsened ±2 ft datum localization from 89.13% to 85.77% and p90 shift from 3.4 ft to 7.0 ft.
implication: Use affine parameters as mismatch diagnostics, not a default GR correction.

claim: Amer's exact second-order HMM provides a deterministic posterior mean/std over joint TVT position and dip rate; its reported 4.57 PF-HMM blend is based on a small sample.
implication: Add HMM outputs to a fresh candidate bank and validate on all frozen maps before promotion.

claim: The public 6.979 notebook and high-vote derivatives combine pretrained artifacts, model packages, overlap contacts, and fixed bias corrections.
implication: Treat their leaderboard scores as composite references, not clean unseen-well causal evidence.

claim: Participants report grouped whole-well pooled CV in the 4.x range using complete-well models and test-time inputs.
implication: Prioritize whole-well nonlinear candidates, but require independent reproduction and frozen controls.

claim: Kaggle currently lists 134 competition topics while the frozen archive contains 132.
implication: Run a complete delta recrawl before changing canonical topic/message counts.
